title: Oscar and the Confession
premise: Insurance investigator Astrid Eastwick is paid an enormous retainer by a nervous client, Oscar Vann, to prove his business partner's death hasn't happened yet — a claim that seems absurd until she finds the partner alive, hiding, and certain Oscar is planning his murder. Astrid realizes the 'case file' Oscar gave her is actually the killer's blueprint, and that whoever orchestrated this scheme wants a murder on record that can be proven impossible. As she races the staged date of death, Astrid discovers Oscar is a coerced pawn protecting a found family of ex-felons his company once exploited, and the true architect is the firm's beloved founder laundering power through manufactured tragedies. In the end, Astrid chooses truth over the loyalty she's come to feel, exposing the founder and giving Oscar's makeshift family a real second chance.
about_author: Silas Okafor is a former claims adjuster from Lagos who spent a decade untangling suspicious deaths for insurers across three continents. He writes mysteries about paper trails, memory, and the people who fall through the gaps between them.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A wealthy, terrified client named Oscar Vann hires her to prove a murder that hasn't happened yet, prepaying a year's fee. Investigating his partner's 'death,' she finds no body — and then the partner, alive and in hiding, insisting Oscar will kill him. The emotional beat is vertigo: Astrid's perfect memory of the case file begins to feel like a script someone wrote for her.

chapters.title: The Blueprint
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, with an interlude in the partner's voice. She realizes the documents Oscar supplied mirror an unsolved murder from a decade ago, down to the timestamps — someone is restaging a crime to launder a new one. When she confronts Oscar, he breaks: he's being blackmailed over the ex-convicts his firm quietly employs. Tension rises as she agrees to help him trap the blackmailer.

chapters.title: The Date of Death
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Astrid and the hidden killer. On the night the file predicts the murder, Astrid stages Oscar's death while staking out the real target. The killer — the firm's revered founder — arrives to finish his design, revealing he's manufactured 'impossible' deaths for years to consolidate power. The climax is a confrontation where Astrid's photographic memory becomes the only evidence that can convict him.

chapters.title: What the Record Keeps
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, closing with Oscar's. Testimony, recordings, and her unerring recall dismantle the founder's empire; the partner resurfaces to testify, and Oscar's makeshift family of second-chance employees survives the scandal. Astrid, who has always trusted records over people, chooses to stand witness for them. The resolution lands on quiet loyalty: truth kept, family found.
